newsitem.title: SPAIN: ATHLETICS-HARRISON AIMING FOR TRIPLE JUMP RECORD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-HARRISON AIMING FOR TRIPLE JUMP RECORD.

text.p: Olympic title-winner Kenny Harrison said on Tuesday that the new track under construction in Athens for the August world championships was likely to produce a triple jump world record.
"I'm looking forward to competing in Athens. There will be some very big distances there and I like very hard tracks," the American said.
"I'd compete on the street or on a cement track if I had the chance and so Athens should be good for me."
The current mark of 18.29 metres was set by Britain's Jonathan Edwards when he won the 1995 world crown.
Harrison, who appears in an indoor grand prix meeting in Madrid on Wednesday, said he was in the best shape of his life, despite only returning to full training after Christmas.
"I really do not like to compete indoors because of the springy floors in most arenas. I tend to get injuries easily, but I feel very good and want to see how my conditioning is going."
He remained undecided about whether he will compete in the world indoor championships in Paris next month despite the introduction of prize money.

"Money has never been a motivating force about whether I compete in a particular place or not. I will be doing some more meetings but I do not even know where I will be competing next because my manager is handling that," he said.
The Madrid event will mark the international reappearance of Britain's Jason Livingston, 1992 European indoor 60 metres champion, since a four-year ban for steroid abuse.
Livingston runs in the 60 metres. He finished his suspension in July and last month won the English national 60 metres title.
